1c272cb165662699ac8a50670acab23e91c8b018: Davos offers 96 km of well-marked runs — a mid-sized ski area ideal for spending 4 to 5 days without ever doing exactly the same thing twice. The 18 lifts are generally enough to handle the crowds in high season. Davos has kept an authentic mountain village identity, far from the concrete resorts of the 1970s. People come here for the clean air, the unspoilt landscapes and a friendly atmosphere that stands apart from the industrialised skiing of some large ski areas. With a summit at 2844 m and a village at 1560 m, snow reliability in Davos is generally good from January to the end of March. A few exceptionally mild winters can cause tension early in the season, but the situation recovers quickly with the first heavy snowfalls. A stay in Davos is clearly a high-budget affair: 91€ for the day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It's the price of excellence — but be aware of it before you go. In short: Davos lives up to its promises. A Northern Alps resort that will suit most profiles without disappointing.
